name: Breadalbane

sources.title: Breadalbane (ship) — barque of 1843, crushed by ice off Beechey Island on 21 August 1853; found in 1980 at about 100 m, intact, two of her three masts standing
The Canadian Encyclopedia — Breadalbane: ice knifed through the starboard bow, sank in 15 minutes; MacInnis found her in 1980; bow pointing east, fractured bowsprit
Parks Canada — Wreck of Breadalbane National Historic Site of Canada (the wreck and its debris field)
Legion Magazine — The world's most northerly shipwreck

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q4959197_breadalbane.py, tools/sailkit.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/dresskit.py) with AI assistance. Upright and intact at about 100 m, bow to the east: two masts still standing with their tops and a few shrouds, the yards hanging askew; the hole cut by the ice in the starboard bow with the frames showing; the helm on the after deck; the fractured bowsprit; the third mast (here the mizzen) fallen over the port quarter, spars and rigging on the bottom; copper sheathing gone green. Which mast fell, the yards and the size of the hole are approximate. model_built.glb: the barque under sail in 1853. No marine life in the model: Offlined draws the living things itself.
